newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse at new record high.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse at new record high.

text.p: The German DAX index of leading shares opened bourse dealings above the magical 2,800 point level for the first time ever on Tuesday, spurred on another record on Wall Street overnight and a firmer dollar.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares reached up to a bourse record high of 2,819.95, before slipping back slightly to stand up 15.22 points, or 0.54 percent, at 2,814.41 by 0951 GMT.
The IBIS DAX index, tracking day-long computer trade in the DAX index, earlier made an all-time high of 2,821.95 points.
"Everyone just keeps buying. We're seeing a cross-the-board rally," said one trader.

Dealers said the stronger dollar, which pulled above the 1.52 mark level late on Monday, was helping the chemical and auto sectors in particular, both of which are export-oriented and benefit from a weaker mark.
In the car sector, BMW and Daimler-Benz AG stocks were both charging ahead, BMW shares gaining 24 marks to 977 marks, and Daimler up 70 pfennigs near to 99.80 marks.
Daimler broke through the 100 mark level in computer dealings, but could not hold above the crucial number.
Amongst the chemical companies, BASF AG, Hoechst AG and Bayer AG were all stronger than the market trend.
Dealers said they saw the current rally continuing until at least the end of the year, with 2,850 points the next major technical resistance level for the DAX to test.
But they said volumes could trail off at the end of the week, with the Thanksgiving public holiday in the U.S on Thursday.
